Average marginal effects for ordinal probabilities

Source: R/marginal-effects.R
fastglm_marginal_effects.Rd

Estimates the average rate of change in each category probability as a continuous predictor changes. Uncertainty uses the delta method, conditional on the supplied predictor values and averaging weights.

fastglm_marginal_effects(
  object,
  variable,
  newdata = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  vcov. = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  type = "response",
  eps = NULL,
  offset = NULL
)

Arguments

object

a converged fastglm_ordinal fit, with common or threshold-specific slopes.

variable

name of one continuous numeric variable. For a formula fit, this names the original variable in the data; interactions and smooth transformations are differentiated together. For a matrix fit, this names one location-design column, with the other columns held fixed.

newdata

data frame for a formula fit, or location-design matrix for a matrix fit. Defaults to retained fitting data. Supply the original variables explicitly when they cannot be recovered from the retained model frame.

weights

nonnegative averaging weights, defaulting to equal weights. Fitting frequency weights are not reused automatically.

vcov.

optional full coefficient covariance matrix, as in fastglm_average().

level

confidence level for separate normal intervals.

type

category probabilities ("response" or "probability") or "cumulative" probabilities.

eps

positive absolute step for numerical differentiation of formula terms. The default is .Machine$double.eps^(1/3) * pmax(1, abs(x)) for the selected variable. Matrix-column derivatives are exact and do not use this argument.

offset

optional replacement prediction offset. All offsets are held fixed when differentiating, including formula offsets involving variable.

Value

A data frame with variable, category, estimate, std.error, conf.low, and conf.high. Category effects sum to zero. Removed categories have zero effects and unavailable standard errors; inference otherwise refers to the reduced category model.

Details

A marginal effect is a derivative, measured in probability units per unit of the continuous predictor. It describes a local rate of change; a finite change can give a different probability difference. Use fastglm_average(contrast = ...) for discrete comparisons, including factors. A numeric binary indicator is treated as continuous if requested.

Formula design derivatives use centered differences, with the fitted prediction basis and factor coding retained. Terms must be smooth functions of each row's predictors, or use a prediction basis frozen during fitting (for example, poly() or splines::ns()). Expressions that recompute sample summaries such as I(x - mean(x)) are unsupported. Rows and perturbed values with positive averaging weight must be finite and within the domain of the formula transformations. A smaller eps may be needed near a transformation's domain boundary.

Derivatives of probabilities and their parameter gradients are analytic conditional on the computed design derivative. The gradient includes uncertainty in both thresholds and slopes. Computation uses blocks of rows and retains the base prediction design, without storing a full array of observation-by-parameter-by-category derivatives. Normal intervals are first-order approximations; the covariance and reduced-category conventions match fastglm_average(). For nonparallel models, each cumulative probability uses its own slope. Evaluation rows must lie within the fitted model's valid predictor domain. Supplied covariance, including cluster covariance, retains covariance among thresholds, common slopes, and threshold-specific slopes.

Examples

set.seed(91)
d <- data.frame(x=rnorm(150))
d$y <- ordered(cut(.5*d$x + rlogis(150), c(-Inf,-.5,.7,Inf)))
fit <- fastglm_ordinal(y ~ x, data=d, firth=TRUE)
fastglm_marginal_effects(fit, "x")
#>   variable    category     estimate   std.error     conf.low   conf.high
#> 1        x (-Inf,-0.5] -0.074409937 0.032765561 -0.138629256 -0.01019062
#> 2        x  (-0.5,0.7]  0.006715711 0.006508746 -0.006041196  0.01947262
#> 3        x  (0.7, Inf]  0.067694226 0.030100717  0.008697905  0.12669055
